# surveyframe

![surveyframe](reference/figures/readme-logo.png)

> **Just here to verify a `.sframe` file’s integrity hash or read its
> amendment log?** **[Verify a file
> now](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/verify/)**.
> No R, no install. It runs entirely in your browser and nothing is
> uploaded.

`surveyframe` is a research-design-first survey package for R. Most
survey tools collect answers and return counts. `surveyframe` begins at
the research design and carries it through to a written results report.

The unit of work is the instrument, a typed `sframe` object that stores
three things together:

1.  **The questions.** Items, choice sets, scales, branching rules, and
    attention checks.
2.  **The analysis plan.** A list of research questions, where each
    question is bound to a named statistical technique and to the
    variables that fill each role in that technique. The plan is written
    during design, before any data arrive.
3.  **The measurement or structural model.** Constructs, indicators, and
    paths for EFA, CFA, CB-SEM, and PLS-SEM.

Because the plan and the model live inside the instrument, you never
have to go back and match up questions, variables, and tests by hand.
Say you’re comparing satisfaction between first-time and repeat
visitors: write that comparison into the plan once, alongside the
questions, and it stays linked to the right variables from then on. When
responses arrive, running the plan is a single step: each result comes
back ready to write up, with a plot, a table, an APA statistic, an
effect size where it applies, a writing prompt, and the reference that
supports it. Plots switch between a colour palette for on-screen use and
a black-and-white palette for print, both checked against WCAG contrast
rules, so the same run produces a journal-ready figure with no separate
step.

The package works offline during examples, tests, vignettes, and checks.
Browser and Shiny entry points use `open = FALSE` or explicit launch
functions, so automated checks do not open a browser.

## Installation

> **0.4.3 is on GitHub, ahead of CRAN.** CRAN carries 0.4.2. The GitHub
> release, 0.4.3, adds fixes found while teaching with it: a frequency
> table for 2 or more variables, choice labels in frequency tables,
> counts and percentages for choice items, and fixes to SurveyBuilder
> and SurveyStudio. Install it with:
>
> ``` r
>
> remotes::install_github("MohammedAliSharafuddin/surveyframe")
> ```
>
> `NEWS.md` lists every fix.

Install from CRAN:

``` r

install.packages("surveyframe")
```

To get changes not yet released to CRAN:

``` r

remotes::install_github("MohammedAliSharafuddin/surveyframe")
```

In an interactive session,
[`library(surveyframe)`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/)
prints a short start-up note with a demo to try, the commands to start
with, and how to cite the package.
`suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(surveyframe))` loads it quietly,
and scripts and rendered documents never show it.

Optional packages are only needed for selected features:

``` r

install.packages(c("shiny", "psych", "googlesheets4", "digest", "MASS", "nnet"))
```

Syntax generation works without installing `lavaan` or `seminr`. Install
those packages when you want to fit the generated CFA, CB-SEM, or
PLS-SEM models.

## Already have data?

`surveyframe` is not a replacement for whatever collection tool your
institution already has approved: Qualtrics, REDCap, Google Forms, or a
paper form typed up afterward. It reads response data as a plain CSV or
`data.frame` from any of them: export from your collection tool, rename
columns to match your instrument’s item IDs (or build the instrument to
match the export), and load it. If you have collected responses in a CSV
or Google Sheet and want to start from the analysis step, build a
minimal instrument that matches your column names and load the data
directly:

``` r

library(surveyframe)

# 1. Describe the items you already collected
cs  <- sframe_choice_set("agree5", 1:5,
        c("Strongly disagree", "Disagree", "Neutral", "Agree", "Strongly agree"))
i1  <- sframe_item("q1", "Item 1", type = "likert", choice_set = "agree5", scale_id = "S")
i2  <- sframe_item("q2", "Item 2", type = "likert", choice_set = "agree5", scale_id = "S")
sc  <- sframe_scale("S", "My scale", items = c("q1", "q2"))
instr <- sframe_instrument("My study", components = list(cs, i1, i2, sc))

# 2. Load your CSV
responses <- read_responses("my_data.csv", instr, strict = FALSE)

# 3. Score and analyse
scored  <- score_scales(responses, instr)
results <- run_analysis_plan(scored, instr)
```

## Documentation workflow

Choose the route that matches what you need:

- **Try it in five minutes:** Learn by example: 22 small surveys.
- **Prefer a visual interface:** SurveyBuilder, SurveyStudio, and the
  dashboard.
- **Build and collect:** Building a survey instrument, then Deploying
  and collecting.
- **Already have responses:** Analysing survey responses.
- **Read the complete case study:** Digital marketing and tourism
  services.

Continue as needed with these:

- Scale reliability and validity
- EFA, CFA, CB-SEM, and PLS-SEM syntax
- Multi-criteria decision analysis
- Small-sample inference
- Text and open-ended response analysis

Read all eleven vignettes inside R with:

``` r

browseVignettes("surveyframe")
```

## An instrument is the research design

``` r

library(surveyframe)

agree5 <- sframe_choice_set(
  "agree5",
  values = 1:5,
  labels = c("Strongly disagree", "Disagree", "Neutral", "Agree", "Strongly agree")
)

visitor_type_choices <- sframe_choice_set(
  "visitor_type",
  values = c("first_time", "repeat"),
  labels = c("First-time visitor", "Repeat visitor")
)

sat_1 <- sframe_item("sat_1", "The service was reliable.",
  type = "likert", choice_set = "agree5", scale_id = "sat")
sat_2 <- sframe_item("sat_2", "The service was responsive.",
  type = "likert", choice_set = "agree5", scale_id = "sat")
sat_3 <- sframe_item("sat_3", "I would recommend the service.",
  type = "likert", choice_set = "agree5", scale_id = "sat")

visitor_type <- sframe_item("visitor_type", "Visitor type", type = "single_choice",
  choice_set = "visitor_type")
sat <- sframe_scale("sat", "Satisfaction", items = c("sat_1", "sat_2", "sat_3"))

instr <- sframe_instrument(
  "Service Survey",
  components = list(
    agree5, visitor_type_choices, sat_1, sat_2, sat_3, visitor_type, sat
  ),
  analysis_plan = list(
    list(
      id                = "RQ1",
      research_question = "Do first-time and repeat visitors differ in satisfaction?",
      family            = "group_comparison",
      method            = "mann_whitney",
      roles             = list(group = "visitor_type", outcome = "sat"),
      options           = list(alpha = 0.05)
    )
  )
)

write_sframe(instr, tempfile(fileext = ".sframe"))

# See the instrument as a survey a respondent would fill in:
export_survey(instr, open = FALSE)
```

[`write_sframe()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/write_sframe.md)
validates the instrument and writes the validated object, including the
validation flag, the analysis plan, and any saved model specifications.
[`export_survey()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/export_survey.md)
renders it as a self-contained HTML survey, the same function covered in
“Visual tools” below.

## Import and score

``` r

responses <- data.frame(
  respondent_id = paste0("R", 1:5),
  sat_1 = c(4, 5, 3, 4, NA),
  sat_2 = c(5, 4, 3, 4, 5),
  sat_3 = c(4, 5, 2, 4, 4),
  visitor_type = c("first_time", "repeat", "first_time", "repeat", "first_time")
)

resp <- read_responses(responses, instr, respondent_id = "respondent_id", strict = FALSE)

score_scales(resp, instr)
sframe_missing_data_results(resp, instr)
```

## Run the analysis plan

Each block binds a research question to a technique and to the variables
that fill each role.
[`run_analysis_plan()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/run_analysis_plan.md)
runs every block and returns one result per question. Earlier `.sframe`
files using `variables` and `test` fields remain compatible.

``` r

results <- run_analysis_plan(resp, instr)
results
```

Supported method IDs include descriptives, missing data, quality checks,
reliability, EFA readiness and solutions, CFA, CB-SEM, and PLS-SEM
syntax, chi-square, Fisher’s exact test, McNemar, Cochran’s Q, t-tests,
Mann-Whitney, Wilcoxon, one- and two-way ANOVA, ANCOVA,
repeated-measures ANOVA, Kruskal-Wallis, Friedman, Pearson, Spearman,
and Kendall correlations, partial correlations, linear and logistic
regression, mediation, and moderation. Each technique reports an APA
statistic, an effect size where it applies, a writing prompt, and the
reference that supports it.

## Render the results report

``` r

render_results(results, instr, output_file = tempfile(fileext = ".html"))
```

The report holds one section per research question, with the APA result,
the writing prompt, a space for the interpretation, and a reference list
compiled from the techniques used.

## Reliability, EFA, and CFA

``` r

if (requireNamespace("psych", quietly = TRUE)) {
  sframe_reliability_results(resp, instr, omega = FALSE)
  sframe_efa_readiness_results(resp, instr)
}

sframe_syntax_cfa(instr)
sframe_syntax_cfa(instr, ordered = TRUE)
```

## Model layer

``` r

model <- sframe_model_spec(
  "model_1",
  "Satisfaction model",
  type = "cb_sem",
  constructs = list(
    sframe_construct("SAT", "Satisfaction", c("sat_1", "sat_2", "sat_3"))
  )
)

instr <- sframe_add_model(instr, model)
sframe_model_json(model)
sframe_syntax_sem(model, instr)
```

## PLS-SEM syntax

``` r

pls_model <- sframe_model_spec(
  "pls_1",
  "Satisfaction and loyalty PLS model",
  type = "pls_sem",
  constructs = list(
    sframe_construct("SAT", "Satisfaction", c("sat_1", "sat_2"), mode = "composite"),
    sframe_construct("LOY", "Loyalty", "sat_3", mode = "single_item")
  ),
  paths = list(sframe_path("SAT", "LOY")),
  options = list(bootstrap = 5000)
)

sframe_syntax_pls(pls_model)
```

## A full study report

``` r

render_report(
  instr,
  data = resp,
  output_file = tempfile(fileext = ".html"),
  include_codebook = TRUE,
  include_quality = TRUE,
  include_missing = TRUE,
  include_descriptives = TRUE,
  include_analysis = TRUE,
  include_models = TRUE
)
```

The built-in HTML fallback does not require Quarto. If the Quarto CLI is
available locally,
[`render_report()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/render_report.md)
can use the bundled template.

## Visual tools

``` r

launch_builder(open = FALSE)
export_survey(instr, open = FALSE)
```

Use
[`launch_builder()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/launch_builder.md)
to author the questionnaire, the plan, and the model and to export the
`.sframe` file and model syntax. It runs no statistics.
[`launch_studio()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/launch_studio.md)
uploads responses, runs the plan on its Analysis Plan screen, and
renders the report on its Export screen. Its Dashboard screen explores
responses with filters. Demo launchers are available for training:

``` r

launch_builder(demo = "input_types", open = FALSE)
# launch_studio(demo = "input_types", screen = "preview")
# launch_studio(demo = "input_types", screen = "dashboard")
```

Interactive functions such as `launch_builder(open = TRUE)`,
[`launch_studio()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/launch_studio.md),
and
[`run_survey()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/run_survey.md)
are available for manual use. Tests and examples avoid opening browsers.

## Roadmap

0.4.0 (CRAN, 2026-08-20) added three capability themes:

- **Small-sample survey helpers**, validated by a simulation study:
  Hodges-Lehmann and paired-Wilcoxon pseudomedian estimators, exact
  Fisher odds-ratio intervals, and Firth logistic regression.
- **10 multi-criteria decision methods** (TOPSIS, AHP, ANP, DEMATEL,
  VIKOR, MOORA, SMART, WASPAS, PROMETHEE, ELECTRE), with 2 new question
  types for collecting judgements, weight-sensitivity analysis, and
  declared conjoint designs.
- **Text and open-ended response analysis**, 9 methods: term and n-gram
  frequency, keyword in context, co-occurrence networks, sentiment,
  document-feature matrices, and topic modelling via LDA or a structural
  topic model.

A disclosed-amendment and Git-linked provenance mechanism shipped
alongside, on top of the existing `.sframe` integrity hash. Full detail
in `NEWS.md`.

0.4.1 focuses on stability: fixes found by using surveyframe on real
instruments, no new capability theme.

0.4.2 is a defect-fix release, correcting what an external review of
0.4.1 found across 8 batches: 171 findings, 154 fixed here and 17
deferred with a stated reason. The ones that matter most to a live study
are in collection, where a participant’s answer could be altered or lost
with no signal, and in scoring, where the report path recomputed scale
scores by a second method that ignored reverse coding and the declared
minimum. Some numbers therefore move between 0.4.1 and 0.4.2, and
`NEWS.md` says which, under “What you need to change”. Reports also
gained a folded “Show R code” block, and
[`sframe_syntax_result()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_syntax_result.md)
returns the statistical call behind a result with its variables and
options resolved, so a reader can copy the code and reproduce the
number.

0.4.3, a GitHub release, fixes what a teaching session found in 0.4.2:
frequency and descriptives blocks now handle choice items as categories,
and SurveyBuilder reads a plan written in R as R does.

## When to use surveyframe, and when not to

surveyframe is a fit when a study’s analysis has to be decided before
data collection: a scale to validate, a pre-registered hypothesis test,
a measurement model to fit, or an audit trail showing the plan wasn’t
changed after seeing results. Its core strength is a pre-declared,
integrity-checked analysis plan bound to the instrument itself. It also
interoperates with [survey](https://cran.r-project.org/package=survey)
and [srvyr](https://cran.r-project.org/package=srvyr), the standard
tools for weighting and variance estimation on data from a complex
probability sample.

Haven’t decided the analysis yet? Collect first with any web-form tool,
Google Forms, Qualtrics, REDCap, or the R package
[surveydown](https://github.com/surveydown-dev/surveydown), and add the
plan when you’re ready: surveyframe reads exported CSV data from any of
them (see “Already have data?” above).

**If this package is ever archived by CRAN**, the GitHub repository
remains the canonical source:
`remotes::install_github("MohammedAliSharafuddin/surveyframe")`. Each
CRAN release is also deposited to Zenodo with its own DOI, so a specific
version stays citable and retrievable independently of both CRAN’s and
GitHub’s continued availability.

## FAQ

**Is surveyframe a replacement for Qualtrics, Google Forms, or REDCap?**
No. Those collect responses with no plan required up front. surveyframe
declares the analysis plan before collection, and reads exported CSV
data from any of them once the plan is added (see “Already have data?”
above).

**Does surveyframe do survey weighting or complex-sample variance
estimation?** No. [survey](https://cran.r-project.org/package=survey)
and [srvyr](https://cran.r-project.org/package=srvyr) are the standard R
tools for stratified, clustered, or weighted samples. surveyframe’s
instruments interoperate with that workflow instead of duplicating it.

**Can I use surveyframe with data I’ve already collected?** Yes. Build a
minimal instrument that matches your column names, then load your CSV or
`data.frame` directly with
[`read_responses()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/read_responses.md).
See “Already have data?” above for a worked example.

**What is a pre-declared analysis plan, and why does it matter?** A list
of research questions written into the instrument at design time, each
bound to a technique and to the variables that fill its roles, before
any response arrives. It removes matching questions, variables, and
tests up by hand, and it’s the basis for the audit trail showing the
plan wasn’t changed after seeing results.

**What happens if surveyframe is ever archived by CRAN?** The GitHub
repository stays the canonical source
(`remotes::install_github("MohammedAliSharafuddin/surveyframe")`), and
every CRAN release is separately deposited to Zenodo with its own DOI.

## Citation

``` r

citation("surveyframe")
```

## Related resources

- Sharafuddin, M. A., Jaleel, A. A., and Madhavan, M. (2026).
  *Quantitative Analysis with Small Samples: A Practical Guide for
  Students and Early-Career Researchers* (Version 0.1.0) \[Book\].
  Zenodo. <https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20221929>. A companion
  textbook on statistical inference when sample sizes are small, also
  available at <https://flairmi.com/textbooks/smallsamplelab.html>. It
  describes the small-sample methods that surveyframe added in 0.4.0 and
  when to prefer each one.
- Sharafuddin, M. A. (2026). *surveyframe: A Pre-Declared, Reproducible
  Framework for Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis in Survey Research*.
  Manuscript in preparation for Computo. Describes the 10 MCDM methods
  surveyframe added in 0.4.0.

# Package index

## Start here

SurveyStudio opens an instrument and takes it through every stage below,
with no code. ?surveyframe is the map of the package, and
sframe_demo(“first_survey”) is a whole survey to start from.

- [`surveyframe`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/surveyframe-package.md)
  [`surveyframe-package`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/surveyframe-package.md)
  : surveyframe: Survey Instrument Workflows for R
- [`launch_studio()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/launch_studio.md)
  : Launch the SurveyStudio interface

## Design

Make the instrument: its questions, choice sets, scales, branching and
attention checks, saved as a portable .sframe file. In SurveyBuilder:
the Build mode. In code:
[`sframe_instrument()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_instrument.md)
and the makers listed here, then
[`write_sframe()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/write_sframe.md).

- [`launch_builder()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/launch_builder.md)
  : Launch the surveyframe visual survey builder
- [`sframe_instrument()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_instrument.md)
  : Create a survey instrument object
- [`sframe_get_study()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_get_study.md)
  : The study an instrument serves
- [`sframe_sampling_methods()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_sampling_methods.md)
  : Sampling methods a study can declare
- [`sframe_item()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_item.md)
  : Define a survey item
- [`sframe_choice_set()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_choice_set.md)
  : Define a reusable choice set
- [`sframe_scale()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_scale.md)
  : Define a scored scale
- [`sframe_branch()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_branch.md)
  : Define a branching rule
- [`sframe_attention_check()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_attention_check.md)
  : Define a design-time survey check
- [`sframe_conjoint_design()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_conjoint_design.md)
  : Declare a choice-experiment (conjoint) design
- [`write_sframe()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/write_sframe.md)
  : Write an instrument to a .sframe file
- [`read_sframe()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/read_sframe.md)
  : Read an instrument from a .sframe file
- [`validate_sframe()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/validate_sframe.md)
  : Validate an instrument object
- [`sframe_validation`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_validation.md)
  : Report on a validation result
- [`as_sframe()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/as_sframe.md)
  : Coerce to an instrument

## Plan

Declare the analysis before the data arrive, so the report shows what
was planned and what was run. In SurveyBuilder: the Plan mode. In
SurveyStudio: Plan, or the Analyse screen. In code:
`sframe_plan(x) <- plan`.

- [`sframe_plan()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_plan.md)
  : Get the pre-declared analysis plan
- [`` `sframe_plan<-`() ``](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_plan-set.md)
  : Set the pre-declared analysis plan
- [`sframe_sample_size_plan()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_sample_size_plan.md)
  : Sample-size and power planning helper

## Preview

See the survey as a respondent meets it, with nothing collected. In
SurveyStudio: the Preview screen. In code:
[`preview_survey()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/preview_survey.md).

- [`preview_survey()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/preview_survey.md)
  : Preview a survey as a respondent sees it
- [`run_survey()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/run_survey.md)
  : Render a survey from an instrument object

## Collect

Send the survey out: a standalone HTML page, optionally saving answers
to a Google Sheet, or a Shiny module inside your own app. In
SurveyBuilder: Export survey, with the Google Sheets settings. In code:
[`export_survey()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/export_survey.md).

- [`export_survey()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/export_survey.md)
  : Export a self-contained static HTML survey
- [`export_google_sheet()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/export_google_sheet.md)
  : Export a survey instrument to Google Sheets collection format
- [`sframe_survey_ui()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_survey_ui.md)
  : Shiny module UI for an embedded survey
- [`sframe_survey_server()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_survey_server.md)
  : Shiny module server for an embedded survey

## Responses

Read the answers back against the instrument, check their quality, and
export them with labels for other software. In SurveyStudio: the
Responses and Quality screens. In code:
[`read_responses()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/read_responses.md).

- [`read_responses()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/read_responses.md)
  : Read and validate survey responses
- [`read_sheet_responses()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/read_sheet_responses.md)
  : Read survey responses from a Google Sheet
- [`export_responses()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/export_responses.md)
  : Write responses to SPSS or Stata with the labels attached
- [`sframe_quality_results()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_quality_results.md)
  : Generate a data quality report for survey responses
- [`sframe_missing_data_results()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_missing_data_results.md)
  : Missing-data report
- [`sframe_outlier_results()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_outlier_results.md)
  : Flag univariate and multivariate outliers

## Analyse

Score the scales and run the plan, block by block. In SurveyStudio: the
Explore, Reliability and Analyse screens. In code:
[`run_analysis_plan()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/run_analysis_plan.md).

- [`run_analysis_plan()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/run_analysis_plan.md)
  : Run a pre-planned analysis from an instrument's analysis plan
- [`score_scales()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/score_scales.md)
  : Score defined scales from survey responses
- [`sframe_descriptives_results()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_descriptives_results.md)
  : Descriptive statistics report
- [`sframe_reliability_results()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_reliability_results.md)
  : Estimate scale reliability from item responses
- [`sframe_item_results()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_item_results.md)
  : Generate item-level diagnostics
- [`sframe_efa_readiness_results()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_efa_readiness_results.md)
  : Prepare a survey instrument for exploratory factor analysis
- [`sframe_efa_solution()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_efa_solution.md)
  : Estimate an exploratory factor solution
- [`sframe_validity_results()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_validity_results.md)
  : Validity report for construct models
- [`sframe_assumption_results()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_assumption_results.md)
  : Assumption-check report
- [`sframe_posthoc_results()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_posthoc_results.md)
  : Post-hoc and pairwise comparison report

## Report

Write up what was run: an HTML, PDF, Word or OpenDocument report or its
Quarto source, a codebook, the figures, and the R code behind each
result. In SurveyStudio: the Report screen. In code:
[`render_report()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/render_report.md).

- [`render_report()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/render_report.md)
  : Render a reproducible survey report
- [`sframe_report_source()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_report_source.md)
  : Recompute and check a report source folder
- [`render_results()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/render_results.md)
  : Render analysis results to a formatted HTML report
- [`sframe_reports`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_reports.md)
  : Choosing a report
- [`sframe_format_result()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_format_result.md)
  : Render one analysis result as the report does
- [`sframe_codebook()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_codebook.md)
  : Generate a survey codebook from an instrument object
- [`sframe_save_figures()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_save_figures.md)
  : Save the charts from an analysis plan as files
- [`sframe_analysis_qmd()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_analysis_qmd.md)
  : Write a Quarto analysis notebook for any instrument

## References

Cite the works an instrument draws on. The references travel in the
.sframe file and the report lists each one once, at the end. In
SurveyStudio: the References screen. In code:
[`sframe_add_references()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_add_references.md).

- [`sframe_reference()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_reference.md)
  : Create a reference
- [`read_bibtex()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/read_bibtex.md)
  : Read references from BibTeX
- [`sframe_add_references()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_add_references.md)
  : Add references to an instrument
- [`sframe_get_references()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_get_references.md)
  : List an instrument's references
- [`sframe_bibliography()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_bibliography.md)
  : Write a bibliography as CSL-JSON

## Amendments

Change an instrument mid-study, on the record: each amendment is logged
with its reason and the hash it replaced. In SurveyStudio: the
Amendments screen. In code:
[`amend_sframe()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/amend_sframe.md).

- [`amend_sframe()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/amend_sframe.md)
  : Record a disclosed amendment to an instrument
- [`sframe_get_amendments()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_get_amendments.md)
  : Read an instrument's amendment log
- [`sframe_drop_items()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_drop_items.md)
  : Drop items from scales or models
- [`sframe_item_flags()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_item_flags.md)
  : Items past the usual cut-offs in a measurement result
- [`sframe_link_git_commit()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_link_git_commit.md)
  : Link an instrument to its current Git commit

## Models and syntax

Declare constructs, paths and covariances, and generate lavaan, seminr
and psych syntax from the instrument.

- [`sframe_model_spec()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_model_spec.md)
  : Create a surveyframe model specification
- [`sframe_construct()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_construct.md)
  : Define a latent or composite construct
- [`sframe_path()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_path.md)
  : Define a structural path between constructs
- [`sframe_covariance()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_covariance.md)
  : Define a covariance between constructs
- [`sframe_indirect_effect()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_indirect_effect.md)
  : Define an indirect effect path
- [`sframe_add_model()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_add_model.md)
  : Add a model specification to an instrument
- [`sframe_validate_model()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_validate_model.md)
  : Validate a surveyframe model specification
- [`sframe_model_json()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_model_json.md)
  : Serialise a model specification to JSON
- [`sframe_model_outline()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_model_outline.md)
  : Create a model reporting template
- [`sframe_syntax_cfa()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_syntax_cfa.md)
  : Generate lavaan CFA syntax from an instrument or a declared model
- [`sframe_syntax_efa()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_syntax_efa.md)
  : Generate EFA planning syntax
- [`sframe_syntax_sem()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_syntax_sem.md)
  : Generate lavaan CB-SEM syntax
- [`sframe_syntax_pls()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_syntax_pls.md)
  : Generate seminr PLS-SEM syntax
- [`sframe_syntax_result()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_syntax_result.md)
  : The R code behind an analysis result

## Decision analysis

Multi-criteria decision analysis. The 10 methods run through the
analysis plan like any other, so the functions here assemble their input
and test how stable a ranking is.

- [`sframe_sensitivity_analysis()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_sensitivity_analysis.md)
  : Test how far a decision ranking moves when the weights are perturbed
- [`sframe_assemble_pairwise()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_assemble_pairwise.md)
  : Assemble per-respondent comparison matrices
- [`sframe_aggregate_judgements()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_aggregate_judgements.md)
  : Aggregate individual judgement matrices
- [`sframe_collected_weights()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_collected_weights.md)
  : Criterion weights collected from respondents
- [`sframe_rated_matrix()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_rated_matrix.md)
  : Build a performance matrix from rated matrix items
- [`sframe_decision_options()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_decision_options.md)
  : Normalise the decision options of an analysis-plan block
- [`sframe_dematel_compute()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_dematel_compute.md)
  : The DEMATEL total-relation classification

## Text analysis

Open-ended answers: term and n-gram frequency, keyword in context, and
quote extraction.

- [`sframe_clean_text()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_clean_text.md)
  : Clean open-ended text responses for analysis
- [`sframe_term_frequency()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_term_frequency.md)
  : Term frequency for open-ended text
- [`sframe_ngram_frequency()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_ngram_frequency.md)
  : N-gram frequency for open-ended text
- [`sframe_term_context()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_term_context.md)
  : Keyword-in-context concordance for open-ended text
- [`sframe_extract_quotes()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_extract_quotes.md)
  : Extract representative quotes for each STM topic

## Confidence intervals

Base-R bootstrap and effect-size confidence intervals, reused across the
inferential runners.

- [`sframe_bootstrap_ci()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_bootstrap_ci.md)
  : Percentile bootstrap confidence interval for a statistic
- [`sframe_cohens_d_ci()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_cohens_d_ci.md)
  : Bootstrap confidence interval for Cohen's d
- [`sframe_cramers_v_ci()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_cramers_v_ci.md)
  : Bootstrap confidence interval for Cramer's V
- [`sframe_eta_sq_ci()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_eta_sq_ci.md)
  : Bootstrap confidence interval for eta squared

## Demos

22 small teaching demos, each doing one job, and 2 larger reference
datasets. Each comes with an instrument and response data, and the
teaching demos with a codebook and the results surveyframe produced. See
the “Learn by example” article.

- [`sframe_list_demos()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_list_demos.md)
  : List the bundled demos
- [`sframe_demo()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_demo.md)
  : Load one bundled demo
- [`sframe_demo_qmd()`](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/reference/sframe_demo_qmd.md)
  : Copy a demo's Quarto notebook so you can run and change it

# Articles

### Start here

Twenty-two small surveys, each doing one job, with the whole path from
the questionnaire to the report. Choose the demo that matches the data
you have rather than the name of a test.

- [Learn by example: 22 small
  surveys](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/articles/learn-by-example.md):

### Survey research workflow

Read these in order. Start with the worked example, then build the
instrument, analyse responses, check reliability and validity, generate
model syntax, and finish with the visual tools.

- [Survey design and live results: a tourism services
  example](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/articles/surveyframe.md):
- [Building a survey instrument: questions, plan, and
  model](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/articles/building-survey-instrument.md):
- [Deploying a survey and collecting responses on free
  hosting](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/articles/deploying-and-collecting.md):
- [Analysing survey responses: running the
  plan](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/articles/analysing-survey-responses.md):
- [Scale reliability and
  validity](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/articles/scale-reliability-validity.md):
- [EFA, CFA, CB-SEM, and PLS-SEM syntax
  generation](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/articles/efa-cfa-sem-pls-syntax.md):
- [The visual workflow: SurveyBuilder, SurveyStudio, and the
  dashboard](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/articles/surveybuilder-gui-overview.md):

### Specialised analyses

Read these when a study calls for them. Small-sample inference covers
studies below the n = 30 threshold, multi-criteria decision analysis
covers ranking alternatives against criteria that compete, and text
analysis covers open-ended survey responses.

- [Small-sample
  inference](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/articles/small-sample.md):
- [Multi-criteria decision
  analysis](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/articles/mcdm-analysis.md):
- [Text and open-ended response
  analysis](https://mohammedalisharafuddin.github.io/surveyframe/articles/text-analysis.md):
